question.text: Consider the above electrochemical cell where a metal electrode (M) is undergoing redox reaction by forming $\mathrm{M}^{+}\left(\mathrm{M} \rightarrow \mathrm{M}^{+}+\mathrm{e}^{-}\right)$. The cation $\mathrm{M}^{+}$is present in two different concentrations $c_{1}$ and $c_{2}$ as shown above. Which of the following statement is correct for generating a positive cell potential?

options.text: If $\mathrm{c}_{1}$ is present at cathode, then $\mathrm{c}_{1}<\mathrm{c}_{2}$.
If $\mathrm{c}_{1}$ is present at anode, then $\mathrm{c}_{1}>\mathrm{c}_{2}$.
If $c_{1}$ is present at cathode, then $c_{1}>c_{2}$.
If $\mathrm{c}_{1}$ is present at anode, then $\mathrm{c}_{1}=\mathrm{c}_{2}$.
